title: Existence of the signed augmented row for one ordered closed family
statement: Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion] with quasi-compact complementary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $A$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and $F$ an ordered positive finite closed family over $i$ as in [def-sfb-signed-closed-row-data]. Then a signed augmented row for $F$ with coefficients $A$, in the precise sense of [def-sfb-signed-closed-row-data], exists. In particular its terms and differential are the actual signed finite-intersection formulas, its restrictions and augmentation are normalized by the actual units, and it has the stated termwise total augmentation for every integer cochain complex. No cover or exactness hypothesis or conclusion is included; this statement constructs no comparison between different families.

proof.text: For every finite intersection use the product projections to construct the arrows for subset inclusion, and for a nonempty intersection its arrow to Z from the supplied factorizations. These are actual scheme arrows, not just inclusions of underlying sets. Empty intersection is X. Finite unions of the quasi-compact complementary opens show the same hypotheses for all intersections.

proof.text: Use actual module inverse/direct images with inverse-image coefficient rings. Push the unit along each intersection arrow and use the unit-normalized composition comparison. Put zero for invalid subset pairs. The composition-unit identity gives the unit equations and restriction composition; the uniqueness of the conjugate comparison and product arrows gives coherence. The same argument gives the maps from Z. Additivity comes from additive inverse image and the sectionwise direct image.

proof.text: Construct the complex with the existing finite ordered terms and differential. For omitted positions u<v the two possible deletions have signs (-1)^(u+v-1) and (-1)^(u+v); their composites equal the same restriction, so each pair cancels. The singleton augmentation followed by the first differential is zero by the same composition equation. All functor maps and their additivity follow from the naturality of the units and the finite product universal property. A strictly increasing (p+1)-tuple cannot exist for p at least m, so that product is the zero object; use zero also in negative degrees.

proof.text: The previous chain equation constructs alpha from the single complex. Apply its degree-zero augmentation termwise to K and include the horizontal degree-zero summand into the total. The horizontal differential kills this augmentation, and its naturality commutes with d_K. Since the vertical sign in horizontal degree zero is one, this defines the total chain augmentation, with exactly the stated component formula. This construction uses no covering hypothesis and no exactness.
